# Comprehensive Coursework Project Plan: Sales Ticket Accounting System

## 1. General Analysis of Requirements

### 1.1. Project Purpose and Educational Goals

- **Primary Objectives:**
  - Reinforce C# programming fundamentals through practical implementation
  - Develop comprehensive skills across the entire software development lifecycle
  - Focus on code quality, testing standards, and thorough documentation
  - Master modern software architecture principles and patterns
  - Gain experience with enterprise-grade development practices

- **Technical Learning Goals:**
  - Master event-driven architecture and reactive programming
  - Implement enterprise integration patterns
  - Develop skills in distributed systems and microservices
  - Practice advanced database design and optimization
  - Learn modern UI/UX development with Avalonia

- **Professional Development:**
  - Understand business process automation
  - Learn project management methodologies
  - Practice documentation and technical writing
  - Develop problem-solving and debugging skills
  - Experience team collaboration workflows

### 1.2. Technology Stack

- **Frontend:** 
  - Avalonia UI 11.0 for cross-platform desktop application
  - ReactiveUI for reactive programming patterns
  - Material.Avalonia for modern UI components
  - FluentUI.Core for consistent design language

- **Backend:** 
  - ASP.NET Core (.NET 9) for API development
  - MediatR for CQRS pattern implementation
  - FluentValidation for robust input validation
  - AutoMapper for object-object mapping

- **Database:** 
  - PostgreSQL 15 for production environment
  - Entity Framework Core for ORM
  - Fluent Migrations for database versioning
  - Dapper for high-performance queries

- **Authentication:** 
  - JWT + ASP.NET Identity for secure authentication
  - IdentityServer4 for OAuth2/OpenID Connect
  - Azure Active Directory integration capability
  - Custom claims-based authorization

- **Reporting:** 
  - QuestPDF for dynamic PDF generation
  - ClosedXML for Excel report generation
  - Chart.js for interactive data visualization
  - Custom reporting engine for flexible templates

- **CI/CD:** 
  - GitHub Actions with SonarCloud for quality gates
  - Docker containers for consistent deployment
  - Azure DevOps integration for enterprise scenarios
  - Automated testing and deployment pipelines

### 1.3. Submission Requirements

- **Formatted and bound explanatory note containing:**
  - Comprehensive system architecture documentation
  - Detailed API specifications and endpoints
  - Database schema and relationships
  - Security implementation details
  - Performance optimization strategies
  - Testing coverage reports

- **Electronic media containing:**
  - Complete source code with Git history
  - Compiled executable files for multiple platforms
  - Comprehensive documentation in markdown format
  - Database scripts and migration files
  - Configuration templates and examples
  - Docker compose files for easy deployment

- **Optional electronic verification (up to 2 weeks before exam)**
  - System demonstration video
  - Live deployment showcase
  - Performance testing results
  - Security audit reports

## 2. System Architecture

### 2.1. Solution Structure
```
TicketSystem/
├── Core/                # Domain models, interfaces
│   ├── Entities/        # Database entities
│   │   ├── Transport/   # Transport-related entities
│   │   ├── Sales/       # Sales-related entities
│   │   ├── Auth/        # Authentication entities
│   │   └── Common/      # Shared entities
│   ├── Interfaces/      # Service contracts
│   │   ├── Services/    # Business service interfaces
│   │   ├── Repos/       # Repository interfaces
│   │   └── Auth/        # Authentication interfaces
│   └── Events/          # Domain events
├── Infrastructure/      # Data access, migrations
│   ├── Data/           
│   │   ├── Context/     # DbContext implementations
│   │   ├── Repos/       # Repository implementations
│   │   └── Migrations/  # EF Core migrations
│   ├── Services/       
│   │   ├── Auth/        # Authentication services
│   │   ├── Email/       # Email services
│   │   └── Storage/     # File storage services
│   └── Configuration/   # Infrastructure configuration
├── Application/        # Business logic
│   ├── Services/       
│   │   ├── Sales/       # Sales processing services
│   │   ├── Reports/     # Reporting services
│   │   └── Admin/       # Administration services
│   ├── DTOs/           
│   │   ├── Requests/    # Input DTOs
│   │   └── Responses/   # Output DTOs
│   └── Validators/      # DTO validators
├── WebApi/             # REST API
│   ├── Controllers/     # API endpoints
│   ├── Middleware/      # Custom middleware
│   ├── Filters/         # Action filters
│   └── Configuration/   # API configuration
├── UI.Avalonia/        # Desktop UI
│   ├── Views/           # XAML views
│   ├── ViewModels/      # View models
│   ├── Services/        # UI-specific services
│   └── Styles/          # UI themes and styles
└── Tests/              # Unit & integration tests
    ├── Unit/            # Unit tests
    ├── Integration/     # Integration tests
    └── UI/              # UI automation tests
```

### 2.2. Database Schema

```sql
-- Core Tables
CREATE TABLE Users (
    Id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    Username VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    PasswordHash VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    Email VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    PhoneNumber VARCHAR(20),
    LastLogin TIMESTAMP,
    CreatedAt TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    UpdatedAt TIMESTAMP,
    IsActive BOOLEAN DEFAULT true,
    RefreshToken VARCHAR(255),
    RefreshTokenExpiryTime TIMESTAMP
);

-- RBAC Tables
CREATE TABLE Roles (
    Id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    Name VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    Description TEXT,
    CreatedAt TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    UpdatedAt TIMESTAMP
);

CREATE TABLE Permissions (
    Id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    Name VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    Description TEXT,
    CreatedAt TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
);

CREATE TABLE RolePermissions (
    RoleId UUID REFERENCES Roles(Id),
    PermissionId UUID REFERENCES Permissions(Id),
    PRIMARY KEY (RoleId, PermissionId)
);

CREATE TABLE UserRoles (
    UserId UUID REFERENCES Users(Id),
    RoleId UUID REFERENCES Roles(Id),
    PRIMARY KEY (UserId, RoleId)
);

-- Core Business Tables
CREATE TABLE Tickets (
    Id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    TransportId UUID NOT NULL,
    Price DECIMAL(10,2) NOT NULL,
    DepartureTime TIMESTAMP NOT NULL,
    ArrivalTime TIMESTAMP NOT NULL,
    Status INT NOT NULL,
    SeatNumber VARCHAR(10),
    BookingReference VARCHAR(20) UNIQUE,
    CreatedAt TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    UpdatedAt TIMESTAMP,
    CreatedBy UUID REFERENCES Users(Id),
    UpdatedBy UUID REFERENCES Users(Id),
    FOREIGN KEY (TransportId) REFERENCES Transports(Id)
);

CREATE TABLE Transports (
    Id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    Model VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
    Seats INT CHECK (Seats > 0),
    Type INT NOT NULL,
    RegistrationNumber VARCHAR(20) UNIQUE,
    ManufactureYear INT,
    LastMaintenanceDate TIMESTAMP,
    NextMaintenanceDate TIMESTAMP,
    Status INT NOT NULL,
    CreatedAt TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    UpdatedAt TIMESTAMP
);

-- Employee Management
CREATE TABLE Jobs (
    Id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    Title VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
    RequiresInternship BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE,
    CreatedAt TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    UpdatedAt TIMESTAMP
);

CREATE TABLE Employees (
    Id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    EmployeeNumber VARCHAR(20) UNIQUE NOT NULL,
    LastName VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
    FirstName VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
    Patronymic VARCHAR(100),
    EmployedSince DATE NOT NULL,
    JobId UUID REFERENCES Jobs(Id),
    CreatedAt TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    UpdatedAt TIMESTAMP
);

-- Bus Management
CREATE TABLE Buses (
    Id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    BusNumber VARCHAR(20) UNIQUE NOT NULL,
    ModelId UUID REFERENCES Transports(Id),
    CreatedAt TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    UpdatedAt TIMESTAMP
);

CREATE TABLE Maintenance (
    Id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    BusId UUID REFERENCES Buses(Id),
    LastMaintenanceDate TIMESTAMP NOT NULL,
    EngineerEmployeeId UUID REFERENCES Employees(Id),
    Issues TEXT,
    NextMaintenanceDate TIMESTAMP NOT NULL,
    Roadworthy BOOLEAN DEFAULT TRUE,
    CreatedAt TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    UpdatedAt TIMESTAMP
);

CREATE TABLE Routes (
    Id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    RouteNumber VARCHAR(20) UNIQUE NOT NULL,
    StartLocation VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    EndLocation VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    DriverEmployeeId UUID REFERENCES Employees(Id),
    AssignedBusId UUID REFERENCES Buses(Id),
    TravelTime INTERVAL NOT NULL,
    CreatedAt TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    UpdatedAt TIMESTAMP
);

CREATE TABLE Sales (
    Id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    SaleDate TIMESTAMP NOT NULL,
    TicketId UUID REFERENCES Tickets(Id),
    CreatedAt TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    UpdatedAt TIMESTAMP
);

-- Document Workflow
CREATE TABLE Documents (
    Id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    Type VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
    Number VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
    Date TIMESTAMP NOT NULL,
    Status VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
    Content JSONB,
    CreatedBy UUID REFERENCES Users(Id),
    ApprovedBy UUID REFERENCES Users(Id),
    CreatedAt TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    UpdatedAt TIMESTAMP
);

CREATE TABLE DocumentWorkflow (
    Id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    DocumentId UUID REFERENCES Documents(Id),
    FromStatus VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
    ToStatus VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
    UserId UUID REFERENCES Users(Id),
    Comment TEXT,
    Timestamp TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
);

-- 1C-Style Metadata Configuration
CREATE TABLE CharacteristicTypes (
    Id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    Name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
    DataType INT NOT NULL,
    TargetEntity VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
    ValidationRule VARCHAR(500),
    IsRequired BOOLEAN DEFAULT false,
    DefaultValue VARCHAR(255),
    CreatedAt TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    UpdatedAt TIMESTAMP
);

CREATE TABLE CharacteristicValues (
    Id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    TypeId UUID REFERENCES CharacteristicTypes(Id),
    EntityId UUID NOT NULL,
    StringValue TEXT,
    NumericValue DECIMAL(18,2),
    DateValue TIMESTAMP,
    BooleanValue BOOLEAN,
    CreatedAt TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    UpdatedAt TIMESTAMP
);

-- Inventory Management
CREATE TABLE Warehouses (
    Id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    Name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
    Address TEXT,
    IsActive BOOLEAN DEFAULT true,
    CreatedAt TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    UpdatedAt TIMESTAMP
);

CREATE TABLE InventoryItems (
    Id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    Name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
    SKU VARCHAR(50) UNIQUE,
    Description TEXT,
    MinimumStock INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    ReorderPoint INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    CreatedAt TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    UpdatedAt TIMESTAMP
);

CREATE TABLE InventoryTransactions (
    Id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    WarehouseId UUID REFERENCES Warehouses(Id),
    ItemId UUID REFERENCES InventoryItems(Id),
    Type VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
    Quantity INT NOT NULL,
    UnitPrice DECIMAL(10,2),
    DocumentId UUID REFERENCES Documents(Id),
    CreatedBy UUID REFERENCES Users(Id),
    CreatedAt TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
);

-- Cartridge Management
CREATE TABLE Cartridges (
    Id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    Model VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
    SerialNumber VARCHAR(50) UNIQUE,
    Status VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
    CurrentLevel INT,
    LastRefillDate TIMESTAMP,
    RefillCount INT DEFAULT 0,
    CreatedAt TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    UpdatedAt TIMESTAMP
);

CREATE TABLE CartridgeHistory (
    Id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    CartridgeId UUID REFERENCES Cartridges(Id),
    Action VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
    Details TEXT,
    PerformedBy UUID REFERENCES Users(Id),
    CreatedAt TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
);

-- Photo Documentation
CREATE TABLE Photos (
    Id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    EntityType VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
    EntityId UUID NOT NULL,
    FilePath VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    FileHash VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL,
    Description TEXT,
    TakenAt TIMESTAMP NOT NULL,
    UploadedBy UUID REFERENCES Users(Id),
    CreatedAt TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
);

-- Telephony Integration
CREATE TABLE CallRecords (
    Id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    CallId VARCHAR(50) UNIQUE,
    CallerNumber VARCHAR(20),
    RecipientNumber VARCHAR(20),
    Duration INT,
    RecordingPath VARCHAR(255),
    Status VARCHAR(20),
    StartTime TIMESTAMP,
    EndTime TIMESTAMP,
    CreatedAt TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
);

CREATE TABLE CallSurveys (
    Id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    CallId UUID REFERENCES CallRecords(Id),
    Rating INT CHECK (Rating BETWEEN 1 AND 5),
    Feedback TEXT,
    SubmittedAt TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
);

-- Audit Logging
CREATE TABLE AuditLogs (
    Id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    UserId UUID REFERENCES Users(Id),
    Action VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
    EntityName VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
    EntityId UUID NOT NULL,
    OldValues JSONB,
    NewValues JSONB,
    Timestamp TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
);

-- OLAP and Analytics
CREATE TABLE SalesAnalytics (
    Id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    TransportId UUID REFERENCES Transports(Id),
    Date DATE NOT NULL,
    TicketsSold INT DEFAULT 0,
    Revenue DECIMAL(18,2) DEFAULT 0,
    OccupancyRate DECIMAL(5,2),
    CreatedAt TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
);

CREATE TABLE AnalyticsCubes (
    Id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    Name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
    Definition JSONB NOT NULL,
    RefreshInterval INT NOT NULL,
    LastRefresh TIMESTAMP,
    CreatedAt TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    UpdatedAt TIMESTAMP
);

-- Localization
CREATE TABLE Languages (
    Id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    Code VARCHAR(10) NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    Name VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
    IsActive BOOLEAN DEFAULT true
);

CREATE TABLE Translations (
    Id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    LanguageId UUID REFERENCES Languages(Id),
    Key VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    Value TEXT NOT NULL,
    Context VARCHAR(50),
    UNIQUE (LanguageId, Key, Context)
);

-- Indexes
CREATE INDEX idx_tickets_transport ON Tickets(TransportId);
CREATE INDEX idx_tickets_status ON Tickets(Status);
CREATE INDEX idx_transport_type ON Transports(Type);
CREATE INDEX idx_characteristics_entity ON CharacteristicValues(EntityId);
CREATE INDEX idx_audit_entity ON AuditLogs(EntityName, EntityId);
CREATE INDEX idx_sales_date ON SalesAnalytics(Date);
CREATE INDEX idx_document_type_status ON Documents(Type, Status);
CREATE INDEX idx_inventory_sku ON InventoryItems(SKU);
CREATE INDEX idx_cartridge_serial ON Cartridges(SerialNumber);
CREATE INDEX idx_photos_entity ON Photos(EntityType, EntityId);
CREATE INDEX idx_call_records_time ON CallRecords(StartTime);
CREATE INDEX idx_translations_key ON Translations(Key);
```

## 3. Functional Specifications

### 3.1. Authorization System

#### Enhanced Role-Based Access Control
- **Granular Permission System**
  - Role hierarchy with inheritance support
  - Custom claims for feature-specific permissions
  - Dynamic permission management
  - Role-based menu visibility

- **Permission Categories**
  - System Administration
  - User Management
  - Transport Management
  - Ticket Operations
  - Report Generation
  - Configuration Management

#### Authentication Flow
1. **Initial Authentication**
   - User provides credentials
   - System validates against stored hashed passwords
   - JWT token issued with role claims
   - Refresh token generated and stored

2. **Token Management**
   - Access token validation on each request
   - Automatic refresh token rotation
   - Token revocation on logout
   - Session management

3. **Security Features**
   - Brute force protection
   - IP-based rate limiting
   - Device fingerprinting
   - Audit logging

### 3.2. Administrator Module

#### User Management
- **Account Operations**
  - CRUD operations for user accounts
  - Bulk user import/export
  - Password reset workflow
  - Account lockout management

- **Role Management**
  - Role creation and assignment
  - Permission template management
  - Role hierarchy configuration
  - Custom claim management

- **Audit System**
  - Detailed action logging
  - Change tracking
  - Session monitoring
  - Security event alerts

#### Data Management
- **Transport Management**
  - Fleet registration and tracking

  - Password complexity rules
  - History enforcement
  - Expiration policies

- **Token Security**
  - JWT encryption
  - Refresh token rotation
  - Token revocation
  - Session management

- **Access Control**

Based on the comprehensive project plan and our previous discussion, here's a complete example of converting the system to SpacetimeDB:

Core Domain Tables:

Core Authorization Reducers:
csharp
public static class AuthReducers
{
    [SpacetimeDB.Reducer]
    public static void RegisterUser(ReducerContext ctx, string login, string passwordHash, string email)
    {
        // Check if user exists
        var existingUser = User.LoginIndex.Filter(login).FirstOrDefault();
        if (existingUser != null)
        {
            throw new Exception("User already exists");
        }

        var user = new User
        {
            identity = ctx.Sender,
            login = login,
            passwordHash = passwordHash,
            email = email,
            isActive = true,
            createdAt = ctx.Time,
            lastLoginAt = 0
        };
        user.Insert();

        // Assign default role
        var defaultRole = Role.NameIndex.Filter("User").FirstOrDefault();
        if (defaultRole != null)
        {
            var userRole = new UserRole
            {
                userIdentity = ctx.Sender,
                roleId = defaultRole.roleId
            };
            userRole.Insert();
        }
    }

    [SpacetimeDB.Reducer]
    public static bool HasPermission(ReducerContext ctx, string permissionName)
    {
        var userRoles = UserRole.UserIdentityIndex.Filter(ctx.Sender);
        
        foreach (var userRole in userRoles)
        {
            var rolePermissions = RolePermission.RoleIdIndex.Filter(userRole.roleId);
            foreach (var rolePermission in rolePermissions)
            {
                var permission = Permission.FindById(rolePermission.permissionId);
                if (permission.name == permissionName && permission.isActive)
                {
                    return true;
                }
            }
        }
        return false;
    }
}
Ticket Management Reducers:
csharp
public static class TicketReducers
{
    [SpacetimeDB.Reducer]
    public static void PurchaseTicket(ReducerContext ctx, uint routeId, string seatNumber)
    {
        // Check permissions
        if (!AuthReducers.HasPermission(ctx, "PURCHASE_TICKET"))
        {
            throw new Exception("Unauthorized: Missing PURCHASE_TICKET permission");
        }

        // Validate route
        var route = Route.FindById(routeId);
        if (route == null)
        {
            throw new Exception("Route not found");
        }

        // Check seat availability
        var existingTicket = Ticket.SeatIndex.Filter((routeId, seatNumber)).FirstOrDefault();
        if (existingTicket != null)
        {
            throw new Exception("Seat already taken");
        }

        // Create ticket
        var ticket = new Ticket
        {
            routeId = routeId,
            seatNumber = seatNumber,
            status = 1, // Active
            purchasedBy = ctx.Sender,
            departureTime = ctx.Time + 3600, // Example: departure in 1 hour
            price = CalculateTicketPrice(route)
        };
        ticket.Insert();
    }

    [SpacetimeDB.Reducer]
    public static void CancelTicket(ReducerContext ctx, uint ticketId)
    {
        var ticket = Ticket.FindById(ticketId);
        if (ticket == null)
        {
            throw new Exception("Ticket not found");
        }

        // Only ticket owner or admin can cancel
        if (ticket.purchasedBy != ctx.Sender && !AuthReducers.HasPermission(ctx, "ADMIN_CANCEL_TICKET"))
        {
            throw new Exception("Unauthorized: Cannot cancel other user's ticket");
        }

        ticket.status = 2; // Cancelled
        Ticket.UpdateById(ticketId, ticket);
    }
}
Fleet Management Reducers:
csharp
public static class FleetReducers
{
    [SpacetimeDB.Reducer]
    public static void AddBus(ReducerContext ctx, string model, uint seats, string regNumber)
    {
        if (!AuthReducers.HasPermission(ctx, "MANAGE_FLEET"))
        {
            throw new Exception("Unauthorized: Missing MANAGE_FLEET permission");
        }

        var bus = new Bus
        {
            model = model,
            seats = seats,
            registrationNumber = regNumber,
            status = 1, // Active
            manufactureYear = 2024,
            lastMaintenanceDate = ctx.Time,
            nextMaintenanceDate = ctx.Time + (90 * 24 * 3600) // 90 days
        };
        bus.Insert();
    }

    [SpacetimeDB.Reducer]
    public static void ScheduleMaintenance(ReducerContext ctx, uint busId, ulong maintenanceDate)
    {
        if (!AuthReducers.HasPermission(ctx, "SCHEDULE_MAINTENANCE"))
        {
            throw new Exception("Unauthorized: Missing SCHEDULE_MAINTENANCE permission");
        }

        var bus = Bus.FindById(busId);
        if (bus == null)
        {
            throw new Exception("Bus not found");
        }

        bus.nextMaintenanceDate = maintenanceDate;
        Bus.UpdateById(busId, bus);
    }
}

uhh how do SpacetimeDB's generated methods even function \
From the documentation, SpacetimeDB generates methods for tables in C# like this:

csharp
[SpacetimeDB.Table]
public partial struct Person
{
    [SpacetimeDB.Column(ColumnAttrs.PrimaryKey)]
    public int Id;
    public string Name;
    public int Age;
}
This generates the following methods 1:

csharp
public partial struct Person
{
    // Insert current instance into table
    public void Insert();

    // Iterate all rows
    public static IEnumerable<Person> Iter();

    // Query with filter expression
    public static IEnumerable<Person> Query(Expression<Func<Person, bool>> filter);

    // Generated for each column:
    public static IEnumerable<Person> FilterByName(string name);
    public static IEnumerable<Person> FilterByAge(int age);

    // For unique/primary key columns:
    public static Person? FindById(int id);
    public static bool DeleteById(int id);
    public static bool UpdateById(int oldId, Person newValue);
}
So when you define a table, SpacetimeDB automatically generates these methods for querying and modifying the data .

For example, to find a user by ID you would do:

csharp
var user = User.FindById(userId);
Rather than writing SQL queries or using Entity Framework .

The key points about these generated methods:

They are created at compile time
They provide type-safe access to the data
They handle all the database operations internally
They use SpacetimeDB's indexing system for performance

First, define the SpacetimeDB tables and reducers:

Create authentication reducers:
csharp
public static class AuthReducers 
{
    [SpacetimeDB.Reducer]
    public static void CreateAuthToken(ReducerContext ctx, string token, ulong expiresAt)
    {
        var authToken = new AuthToken {
            token = token,
            userIdentity = ctx.Sender,
            expiresAt = expiresAt
        };
        authToken.Insert();
    }

    [SpacetimeDB.Reducer]
    public static void ValidateCredentials(ReducerContext ctx, string login, string passwordHash)
    {
        var user = User.FilterByLogin(login).FirstOrDefault();
        if (user == null || user.passwordHash != passwordHash)
        {
            throw new Exception("Invalid credentials");
        }
    }
}
Modify the existing AuthController to work with SpacetimeDB:
csharp
[ApiController]
[Route("api/[controller]")]
public class AuthController : ControllerBase
{
    private readonly ISpacetimeDBClient _spacetimeDB;
    private readonly IConfiguration _configuration;

    public AuthController(ISpacetimeDBClient spacetimeDB, IConfiguration configuration)
    {
        _spacetimeDB = spacetimeDB;
        _configuration = configuration;
    }

    [Route("login")]
    [HttpPost]
    [AllowAnonymous]
    public async Task<ActionResult<string>> Login([FromBody] LoginModel model)
    {
        try 
        {
            // First validate credentials in SpacetimeDB
            await _spacetimeDB.CallReducer("ValidateCredentials", model.Login, HashPassword(model.Password));

            // If validation succeeds, generate JWT token
            var token = GenerateJwtToken(model.Login);

            // Store token in SpacetimeDB
            var expiresAt = DateTimeOffset.UtcNow.AddHours(1).ToUnixTimeMilliseconds();
            await _spacetimeDB.CallReducer("CreateAuthToken", token, expiresAt);

            return Ok(new { token });
        }
        catch (Exception ex)
        {
            return Unauthorized(new { message = "Invalid username or password" });
        }
    }

    private string GenerateJwtToken(string login)
    {
        // Keep your existing JWT generation logic
        var tokenHandler = new JwtSecurityTokenHandler();
        var key = Encoding.ASCII.GetBytes(_configuration["JwtSettings:Secret"]);
        var tokenDescriptor = new SecurityTokenDescriptor
        {
            Subject = new ClaimsIdentity(new[]
            {
                new Claim(ClaimTypes.Name, login)
            }),
            Expires = DateTime.UtcNow.AddHours(1),
            SigningCredentials = new SigningCredentials(
                new SymmetricSecurityKey(key), 
                SecurityAlgorithms.HmacSha256Signature)
        };

        var token = tokenHandler.CreateToken(tokenDescriptor);
        return tokenHandler.WriteToken(token);
    }
}
Add SpacetimeDB client configuration in Startup.cs:
csharp
public void ConfigureServices(IServiceCollection services)
{
    // Existing configurations
    services.AddControllers();
    services.AddAuthentication(JwtBearerDefaults.AuthenticationScheme)
        .AddJwtBearer(/* your existing JWT config */);

    // Add SpacetimeDB client
    services.AddSingleton<ISpacetimeDBClient>(sp =>
    {
        var config = sp.GetRequiredService<IConfiguration>();
        return new SpacetimeDBClient(config["SpacetimeDB:Address"]);
    });
}
Create a middleware to validate tokens against SpacetimeDB:
csharp
public class SpacetimeDBAuthMiddleware
{
    private readonly RequestDelegate _next;
    private readonly ISpacetimeDBClient _spacetimeDB;

    public SpacetimeDBAuthMiddleware(RequestDelegate next, ISpacetimeDBClient spacetimeDB)
    {
        _next = next;
        _spacetimeDB = spacetimeDB;
    }

    public async Task InvokeAsync(HttpContext context)
    {
        var token = context.Request.Headers["Authorization"]
            .FirstOrDefault()?.Split(" ").Last();

        if (token != null)
        {
            // Query SpacetimeDB for token validity
            var authToken = await _spacetimeDB.Query<AuthToken>()
                .Where(t => t.token == token && t.expiresAt > DateTimeOffset.UtcNow.ToUnixTimeMilliseconds())
                .FirstOrDefaultAsync();

            if (authToken != null)
            {
                // Token is valid in SpacetimeDB
                context.Items["UserIdentity"] = authToken.userIdentity;
            }
        }

        await _next(context);
    }
}
This hybrid approach:

Keeps your existing API endpoints and JWT authentication
Uses SpacetimeDB for data storage and validation
Maintains compatibility with your existing client
Allows gradual migration to SpacetimeDB
You can gradually move more functionality to SpacetimeDB reducers while keeping the API facade for client compatibility.

how does SpacetimeDB.Query in client sdk code work
For the C# client SDK, querying works through generated methods for each table. Here's how:

First you need to subscribe to the table data you want to query:
csharp
SpacetimeDBClient.instance.Subscribe(new List<string> { "SELECT * FROM User" });
1

Once subscribed, you can query the table using generated methods:
csharp
// Iterate all rows
foreach (var user in User.Iter()) {
    Console.WriteLine($"User: {user.Name}");
}
For filtering by specific columns, the SDK generates methods like:
csharp
// Filter by column value
public static IEnumerable<TABLE> FilterBySender(COLUMNTYPE value);
For unique/primary key columns, you get find methods:
csharp
// Find by unique column
public static TABLE? FindBySender(COLUMNTYPE value);
The key points about querying in SpacetimeDB:

You must first subscribe to the data you want to query
The SDK maintains a local client cache of subscribed data
All operations work only on the subscribed data in the cache
SpacetimeDB does not support foreign key constraints, so you need to manually subscribe to all related tables
The documentation recommends optimizing network performance by selecting as few rows as possible in your Subscribe query. Operations that need the entire database state are better run inside modules .

so check and analyze this whole text Okay, I've reviewed the messagespacetime.txt file, SpacetimeDB documentation, and our prior discussion. I'll create a comprehensive, step-by-step guide for migrating your SQL Server-based API server to SpacetimeDB, keeping your existing authentication/authorization system intact (for now), and minimizing disruption to your client applications. This will be a hybrid approach, focusing on a gradual, iterative transition.

CRITICAL UNDERSTANDINGS (REITERATED):

SpacetimeDB is NOT a drop-in replacement for SQL Server. It's a fundamentally different architecture. This means no ORM (EF Core), no foreign keys, no joins, and all data modifications happen through reducers.

Reducers are EVERYTHING. All inserts, updates, and deletes must go through reducers. Reducers are C# functions that run inside the SpacetimeDB server, ensuring data consistency and atomicity.

Identity is for USERS. The built-in Identity type is specifically for user authentication and session management within SpacetimeDB. Do not use it for things like BusId, RouteId, TicketId, etc. Use uint for those.

No automatic RBAC. SpacetimeDB does not have a built-in role-based access control system (yet). You'll implement your own using tables (like Role, Permission, UserRole, RolePermission) and enforce authorization checks within your reducers.

No Joins: Because SpacetimeDB uses structs and the documentation never mentions Join operations, we cannot use Joins in spacetimedb

Hybrid Approach is ESSENTIAL. We will initially dual-write to both SQL Server (using your existing EF Core code) and SpacetimeDB (using reducers). This allows for:

Validation: You can compare the data in both databases to ensure consistency.

Rollback: If something goes wrong with SpacetimeDB, you can easily fall back to SQL Server.

Gradual Migration: You can migrate controllers and client application functionality one piece at a time.

Legacy ID Preservation: We'll add Legacy{Entity}Id fields (e.g., LegacyUserId, LegacyRoleId) to your SpacetimeDB tables to store your original SQL Server primary keys. This allows your existing client code (which might use these numeric IDs) to continue working during the migration.

API Facade: Your ASP.NET Core API will initially act as a facade over SpacetimeDB. Clients will continue to use the same API endpoints and JWT authentication. The API server will translate these requests into SpacetimeDB reducer calls and queries.

Migration Steps:

Step 1: Project Setup and SpacetimeDB Installation

Install SpacetimeDB: Follow the instructions at https://spacetimedb.com/docs/getting-started to install the SpacetimeDB server and CLI. Make sure you can run spacetime start and spacetime server set http://localhost:3000.

Create a C# Module Project: Create a new C# class library project (e.g., TicketSalesModule). This will contain your SpacetimeDB table definitions and reducers.

Add SpacetimeDB NuGet Package: Add the SpacetimeDB.Api NuGet package to your TicketSalesModule project.

Create spacetimedb.toml: In the root of your TicketSalesModule project, create a file named spacetimedb.toml with the following content:

name = "ticket_sales"
version = "0.1.0"
authors = ["Your Name"]

[module]
name_override = "ticket_sales" # Use a consistent name

[dependencies]
# No external dependencies in this example (yet)
Use code with caution.

C#
Atomic Counter Tables (Critical):
SpacetimeDB doesn't have auto-incrementing fields in the same way as SQL Server. We need to implement our own counters, and we do this using a separate table for each auto-incrementing ID. This is absolutely critical for correct operation.

// In the SAME FILE as your table definitions (Module.cs), or a separate file.
// But it MUST be within the same C# project (TicketSalesModule).

[Table] public partial struct UserIdCounter { [Column(ColumnAttrs.PrimaryKey)] public string Key = "userId"; public uint NextId; }
[Table] public partial struct RoleIdCounter { [Column(ColumnAttrs.PrimaryKey)] public string Key = "roleId"; public uint NextId; }
[Table] public partial struct PermissionIdCounter { [Column(ColumnAttrs.PrimaryKey)] public string Key = "permissionId"; public uint NextId; }

Important Notes on Table Definitions:

Identity: The UserProfile table uses Identity as its primary key. This is required for SpacetimeDB's authentication system. You will not use a numeric UserId as the primary key for UserProfile.

LegacyUserId: The UserProfile table includes a LegacyUserId field. This will store the original long UserId from your SQL Server database. This is crucial for maintaining compatibility with your existing API and client applications during the migration. It has the [Column(ColumnAttrs.Unique)] attribute to enforce uniqueness.

Auto-Incrementing IDs: For other tables (like Bus, Route, Ticket), we use uint as the primary key type. SpacetimeDB does not have built-in auto-incrementing IDs. We use the atomic counter pattern (separate tables like BusIdCounter) and the GetNextId helper function to generate unique IDs.

No Foreign Key Constraints: SpacetimeDB doesn't enforce foreign keys. You'll need to validate relationships within your reducer logic (I'll show this in the reducer examples).

Data Types: I've used appropriate SpacetimeDB data types. Note the use of ulong for timestamps (milliseconds since the Unix epoch). decimal is not supported; use double for currency.

Arrays: SpacetimeDB does support arrays of primitive types. I've used string[] in RouteSchedule for RouteStops, DaysOfWeek, etc. This is a good fit for your data.

Denormalization: I've included an example of denormalization (BusModel in Route). This can improve query performance by avoiding the need to query multiple tables. You can add other denormalized fields as needed.

Required Attribute: I've removed most of the explicit [Required] attributes that you had on the SQL models. In SpacetimeDB, fields within structs are implicitly required unless you make them nullable (e.g., string?, ulong?). SpacetimeDB does not allow null values in non-primary key fields unless they are explicitly nullable. Only add ? if a field can truly be missing.

No Navigation Properties: SpacetimeDB doesn't use navigation properties like EF Core. Relationships are managed through explicit foreign key fields (like DriverId, BusId in the Route table) and queries.

Step 3: Implement Reducers (C#)

Reducers are the only way to modify data in SpacetimeDB. They are C# functions that run on the server. This ensures data consistency and atomicity. All reducers should be inside your Module class.

I'll provide complete, ready-to-use reducer examples for the most critical operations. I'll include:

Input Validation: Checking for nulls, empty strings, valid ranges, etc.

Relationship Enforcement: Checking that related records exist (e.g., checking if a RouteId is valid before creating a Ticket).

Authorization: Basic authorization checks (e.g., checking if the caller has the "admin" role). You'll need to adapt this to your specific permission system.

Error Handling: Throwing SpacetimeDBException for errors.

Atomic Counter Usage: Using the GetNextId function for auto-incrementing IDs.

Timestamp Handling: Using ctx.Time.ToUnixTimeMilliseconds() for timestamps.

Transactionality - because reducers are transactions and are atomic

Here's a substantial set of reducers to get you started, covering user management, roles, permissions, and some basic fleet and ticket operations. This is not exhaustive, but it shows the patterns you'll use for all your other reducers.
The SpacetimeDB client SDK provides several ways to query data:

First, you must subscribe to the table data you want to query 1:
csharp
// Subscribe to table data
SpacetimeDBClient.instance.Subscribe(new List<string> { "SELECT * FROM User" });
Once subscribed, you can use the generated methods 2:
csharp
// Iterate all rows in a table
public static IEnumerable<Person> Iter();

// Query with a filter expression 
public static IEnumerable<Person> Query(Expression<Func<Person, bool>> filter);

// Find by primary key
public static Person? FindById(int id);
For filtering by specific columns, the SDK generates methods like :
csharp
public static IEnumerable<Person> FilterByName(string name);
public static IEnumerable<Person> FilterByAge(int age); 
The key things to understand about querying in SpacetimeDB are 13:

You must subscribe to data before querying it
The SDK maintains a local client cache of subscribed data
All operations work on the cached data
No foreign key constraints or joins are supported
For optimal performance, you should:

Subscribe to the minimum data needed 1
Use filters to limit the data returned 2
Run complex queries inside modules rather than in the client 1

Okay, I've reviewed the messagespacetime.txt file, SpacetimeDB documentation, and our prior discussion. I'll create a comprehensive, step-by-step guide for migrating your SQL Server-based API server to SpacetimeDB, keeping your existing authentication/authorization system intact (for now), and minimizing disruption to your client applications. This will be a hybrid approach, focusing on a gradual, iterative transition.

CRITICAL UNDERSTANDINGS (REITERATED):

SpacetimeDB is NOT a drop-in replacement for SQL Server. It's a fundamentally different architecture. This means no ORM (EF Core), no foreign keys, no joins, and all data modifications happen through reducers.

Reducers are EVERYTHING. All inserts, updates, and deletes must go through reducers. Reducers are C# functions that run inside the SpacetimeDB server, ensuring data consistency and atomicity.

Identity is for USERS. The built-in Identity type is specifically for user authentication and session management within SpacetimeDB. Do not use it for things like BusId, RouteId, TicketId, etc. Use uint for those.

No automatic RBAC. SpacetimeDB does not have a built-in role-based access control system (yet). You'll implement your own using tables (like Role, Permission, UserRole, RolePermission) and enforce authorization checks within your reducers.

No Joins: Because SpacetimeDB uses structs and the documentation never mentions Join operations, we cannot use Joins in spacetimedb

Hybrid Approach is ESSENTIAL. We will initially dual-write to both SQL Server (using your existing EF Core code) and SpacetimeDB (using reducers). This allows for:

Validation: You can compare the data in both databases to ensure consistency.

Rollback: If something goes wrong with SpacetimeDB, you can easily fall back to SQL Server.

Gradual Migration: You can migrate controllers and client application functionality one piece at a time.

Legacy ID Preservation: We'll add Legacy{Entity}Id fields (e.g., LegacyUserId, LegacyRoleId) to your SpacetimeDB tables to store your original SQL Server primary keys. This allows your existing client code (which might use these numeric IDs) to continue working during the migration.

API Facade: Your ASP.NET Core API will initially act as a facade over SpacetimeDB. Clients will continue to use the same API endpoints and JWT authentication. The API server will translate these requests into SpacetimeDB reducer calls and queries.

Migration Steps:

Step 1: Project Setup and SpacetimeDB Installation

Install SpacetimeDB: Follow the instructions at https://spacetimedb.com/docs/getting-started to install the SpacetimeDB server and CLI. Make sure you can run spacetime start and spacetime server set http://localhost:3000.

Create a C# Module Project: Create a new C# class library project (e.g., TicketSalesModule). This will contain your SpacetimeDB table definitions and reducers.

Add SpacetimeDB NuGet Package: Add the SpacetimeDB.Api NuGet package to your TicketSalesModule project.

Create spacetimedb.toml: In the root of your TicketSalesModule project, create a file named spacetimedb.toml with the following content:

				counter.Update();
			}
			return counter.NextId;
        } else {
            return 0;
        }
    }
Use code with caution.
C#
Important Notes on Table Definitions:

Identity: The UserProfile table uses Identity as its primary key. This is required for SpacetimeDB's authentication system. You will not use a numeric UserId as the primary key for UserProfile.

LegacyUserId: The UserProfile table includes a LegacyUserId field. This will store the original long UserId from your SQL Server database. This is crucial for maintaining compatibility with your existing API and client applications during the migration. It has the [Column(ColumnAttrs.Unique)] attribute to enforce uniqueness.

Auto-Incrementing IDs: For other tables (like Bus, Route, Ticket), we use uint as the primary key type. SpacetimeDB does not have built-in auto-incrementing IDs. We use the atomic counter pattern (separate tables like BusIdCounter) and the GetNextId helper function to generate unique IDs.

No Foreign Key Constraints: SpacetimeDB doesn't enforce foreign keys. You'll need to validate relationships within your reducer logic (I'll show this in the reducer examples).

Data Types: I've used appropriate SpacetimeDB data types. Note the use of ulong for timestamps (milliseconds since the Unix epoch). decimal is not supported; use double for currency.

Arrays: SpacetimeDB does support arrays of primitive types. I've used string[] in RouteSchedule for RouteStops, DaysOfWeek, etc. This is a good fit for your data.

Denormalization: I've included an example of denormalization (BusModel in Route). This can improve query performance by avoiding the need to query multiple tables. You can add other denormalized fields as needed.

Required Attribute: I've removed most of the explicit [Required] attributes that you had on the SQL models. In SpacetimeDB, fields within structs are implicitly required unless you make them nullable (e.g., string?, ulong?). SpacetimeDB does not allow null values in non-primary key fields unless they are explicitly nullable. Only add ? if a field can truly be missing.

No Navigation Properties: SpacetimeDB doesn't use navigation properties like EF Core. Relationships are managed through explicit foreign key fields (like DriverId, BusId in the Route table) and queries.

Step 3: Implement Reducers (C#)

Reducers are the only way to modify data in SpacetimeDB. They are C# functions that run on the server. This ensures data consistency and atomicity. All reducers should be inside your Module class.

I'll provide complete, ready-to-use reducer examples for the most critical operations. I'll include:

Input Validation: Checking for nulls, empty strings, valid ranges, etc.

Relationship Enforcement: Checking that related records exist (e.g., checking if a RouteId is valid before creating a Ticket).

Authorization: Basic authorization checks (e.g., checking if the caller has the "admin" role). You'll need to adapt this to your specific permission system.

Error Handling: Throwing SpacetimeDBException for errors.

Atomic Counter Usage: Using the GetNextId function for auto-incrementing IDs.

Timestamp Handling: Using ctx.Time.ToUnixTimeMilliseconds() for timestamps.

Transactionality - because reducers are transactions and are atomic

Here's a substantial set of reducers to get you started, covering user management, roles, permissions, and some basic fleet and ticket operations. This is not exhaustive, but it shows the patterns you'll use for all your other reducers.

# BRU-Avtopark-Avtobusov Project Documentation

## Project Overview
This is a comprehensive bus fleet management system built with a layered architecture, consisting of Core models, Services layer, Admin Server API, and UI components.

## Core Models

### User Management

#### User (User.cs)
- **Primary Key**: UserId (long)
- **GUID Identifier**: GuidId
- **Properties**:
  - Login (required)
  - PasswordHash (required)
  - Role (legacy: 0 = User, 1 = Admin)
  - CreatedAt
  - LastLoginAt
  - IsActive
  - UserRoles (navigation property)

#### Roles (Roles.cs)
- **Primary Key**: RoleId (Guid)
- **Properties**:
  - LegacyRoleId (int)
  - Name (required)
  - Description (required)
  - IsActive
  - CreatedAt/UpdatedAt
  - CreatedBy/UpdatedBy
  - NormalizedName
  - IsSystem
  - Priority
  - RolePermissions/UserRoles (navigation)

#### Permissions (Permissions.cs)
- **Primary Key**: PermissionId (Guid)
- **Properties**:
  - Name (required, max 50 chars)
  - Description (required, max 200 chars)
  - Category (required)
  - IsActive
  - CreatedAt

### Fleet Management

#### Bus (Avtobus.cs)
- **Primary Key**: BusId (long)
- **Properties**:
  - Model (required)
  - Routes (navigation)
  - Obsluzhivanies (maintenance records)

#### Maintenance (Obsluzhivanie.cs)
- **Primary Key**: MaintenanceId (long)
- **Properties**:
  - BusId (foreign key)
  - LastServiceDate
  - ServiceEngineer
  - FoundIssues
  - NextServiceDate
  - Roadworthiness

#### Route (Marshut.cs)
- **Primary Key**: RouteId (long)
- **Properties**:
  - StartPoint (required)
  - EndPoint (required)
  - DriverId (foreign key)
  - BusId (foreign key)
  - TravelTime
  - Tickets (navigation)

### Employee Management

  - Surname (required)

- **Primary Key**: SaleId (long)

  - SaleDate

    PhoneNumber VARCHAR(20),
    LastLogin TIMESTAMP,
    CreatedAt TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,

);

    UpdatedAt TIMESTAMP

    CreatedAt TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP

    PRIMARY KEY (RoleId, PermissionId)

Core Architecture Changes:
SpacetimeDB will replace both PostgreSQL and Entity Framework Core 1
All data modifications must happen through reducers (no direct SQL queries)
No ORM or navigation properties like in EF Core
No foreign key constraints - relationships must be managed in reducer logic
Data Type Mapping:
SpacetimeDB supports these types :

Basic types (bool, byte, short, int, uint, long, ulong, float, double, string)
Arrays of supported types
List and Dictionary<TKey,TValue>
Identity type for user authentication
Address type for connection management

The hybrid approach would involve:

Keep existing ASP.NET Core API as facade

Maintain JWT token handling in API layer

based on entire chat history and text below analyze for how correrct the plan looks 
Okay, I've reviewed the messagespacetime.txt file, SpacetimeDB documentation, and our prior discussion. I'll create a comprehensive, step-by-step guide for migrating your SQL Server-based API server to SpacetimeDB, keeping your existing authentication/authorization system intact (for now), and minimizing disruption to your client applications. This will be a hybrid approach, focusing on a gradual, iterative transition.

CRITICAL UNDERSTANDINGS (REITERATED):

SpacetimeDB is NOT a drop-in replacement for SQL Server. It's a fundamentally different architecture. This means no ORM (EF Core), no foreign keys, no joins, and all data modifications happen through reducers.

Reducers are EVERYTHING. All inserts, updates, and deletes must go through reducers. Reducers are C# functions that run inside the SpacetimeDB server, ensuring data consistency and atomicity.

Identity is for USERS. The built-in Identity type is specifically for user authentication and session management within SpacetimeDB. Do not use it for things like BusId, RouteId, TicketId, etc. Use uint for those.

No automatic RBAC. SpacetimeDB does not have a built-in role-based access control system (yet). You'll implement your own using tables (like Role, Permission, UserRole, RolePermission) and enforce authorization checks within your reducers.

No Joins: Because SpacetimeDB uses structs and the documentation never mentions Join operations, we cannot use Joins in spacetimedb

Hybrid Approach is ESSENTIAL. We will initially dual-write to both SQL Server (using your existing EF Core code) and SpacetimeDB (using reducers). This allows for:

Validation: You can compare the data in both databases to ensure consistency.

Rollback: If something goes wrong with SpacetimeDB, you can easily fall back to SQL Server.

Gradual Migration: You can migrate controllers and client application functionality one piece at a time.

Legacy ID Preservation: We'll add Legacy{Entity}Id fields (e.g., LegacyUserId, LegacyRoleId) to your SpacetimeDB tables to store your original SQL Server primary keys. This allows your existing client code (which might use these numeric IDs) to continue working during the migration.

API Facade: Your ASP.NET Core API will initially act as a facade over SpacetimeDB. Clients will continue to use the same API endpoints and JWT authentication. The API server will translate these requests into SpacetimeDB reducer calls and queries.

Migration Steps:

Step 1: Project Setup and SpacetimeDB Installation

Install SpacetimeDB: Follow the instructions at https://spacetimedb.com/docs/getting-started to install the SpacetimeDB server and CLI. Make sure you can run spacetime start and spacetime server set http://localhost:3000.

Create a C# Module Project: Create a new C# class library project (e.g., TicketSalesModule). This will contain your SpacetimeDB table definitions and reducers.

Add SpacetimeDB NuGet Package: Add the SpacetimeDB.Api NuGet package to your TicketSalesModule project.

Create spacetimedb.toml: In the root of your TicketSalesModule project, create a file named spacetimedb.toml with the following content:

name = "ticket_sales"
version = "0.1.0"
authors = ["Your Name"]

[module]
name_override = "ticket_sales" # Use a consistent name

[dependencies]
# No external dependencies in this example (yet)
Use code with caution.

Atomic Counter Tables (Critical):
SpacetimeDB doesn't have auto-incrementing fields in the same way as SQL Server. We need to implement our own counters, and we do this using a separate table for each auto-incrementing ID. This is absolutely critical for correct operation.

// In the SAME FILE as your table definitions (Module.cs), or a separate file.
// But it MUST be within the same C# project (TicketSalesModule).

[Table] public partial struct UserIdCounter { [Column(ColumnAttrs.PrimaryKey)] public string Key = "userId"; public uint NextId; }
[Table] public partial struct RoleIdCounter { [Column(ColumnAttrs.PrimaryKey)] public string Key = "roleId"; public uint NextId; }
[Table] public partial struct PermissionIdCounter { [Column(ColumnAttrs.PrimaryKey)] public string Key = "permissionId"; public uint NextId; }
[Table] public partial struct BusIdCounter { [Column(ColumnAttrs.PrimaryKey)] public string Key = "busId"; public uint NextId; }
[Table] public partial struct MaintenanceIdCounter { [Column(ColumnAttrs.PrimaryKey)] public string Key = "maintenanceId"; public uint NextId; }
[Table] public partial struct RouteIdCounter { [Column(ColumnAttrs.PrimaryKey)] public string Key = "routeId"; public uint NextId; }
[Table] public partial struct ScheduleIdCounter { [Column(ColumnAttrs.PrimaryKey)] public string Key = "scheduleId"; public uint NextId; }
[Table] public partial struct EmployeeIdCounter { [Column(ColumnAttrs.PrimaryKey)] public string Key = "employeeId"; public uint NextId; }
[Table] public partial struct JobIdCounter { [Column(ColumnAttrs.PrimaryKey)] public string Key = "jobId"; public uint NextId; }
[Table] public partial struct TicketIdCounter { [Column(ColumnAttrs.PrimaryKey)] public string Key = "ticketId"; public uint NextId; }
[Table] public partial struct SaleIdCounter { [Column(ColumnAttrs.PrimaryKey)] public string Key = "saleId"; public uint NextId; }
[Table] public partial struct LogIdCounter { [Column(ColumnAttrs.PrimaryKey)] public string Key = "logId"; public uint NextId; }

// Helper function to get the next ID from a counter table (used in reducers).
// This function MUST be `private static` and within the `Module` class.

   private static uint GetNextId(string counterKey)
    {
        // Use if-else if blocks for comparison of string keys.
		if (counterKey == "userId") {
			var counter = UserIdCounter.Query().FirstOrDefault();
			if (counter == null) {
				counter = new UserIdCounter { NextId = 1 };
				counter.Insert();
			} else {
				counter.NextId++;
				counter.Update();
			}
			return counter.NextId;
		} else if (counterKey == "roleId") {
            var counter = RoleIdCounter.Query().FirstOrDefault();
			if (counter == null) {
				counter = new RoleIdCounter { NextId = 1 };
				counter.Insert();
			} else {
				counter.NextId++;
				counter.Update();
			}
			return counter.NextId;
        }
		else if (counterKey == "permissionId") {
            var counter = PermissionIdCounter.Query().FirstOrDefault();
			if (counter == null) {
				counter = new PermissionIdCounter { NextId = 1 };
				counter.Insert();
			} else {
				counter.NextId++;
				counter.Update();
			}
			return counter.NextId;
        }
		else if (counterKey == "busId") {
           var counter = BusIdCounter.Query().FirstOrDefault();
			if (counter == null) {
				counter = new BusIdCounter { NextId = 1 };
				counter.Insert();
			} else {
				counter.NextId++;
				counter.Update();
			}
			return counter.NextId;
        }
		else if (counterKey == "maintenanceId") {
           var counter = MaintenanceIdCounter.Query().FirstOrDefault();
			if (counter == null) {
				counter = new MaintenanceIdCounter { NextId = 1 };
				counter.Insert();
			} else {
				counter.NextId++;
				counter.Update();
			}
			return counter.NextId;
        }
		else if (counterKey == "routeId") {
           var counter = RouteIdCounter.Query().FirstOrDefault();
			if (counter == null) {
				counter = new RouteIdCounter { NextId = 1 };
				counter.Insert();
			} else {
				counter.NextId++;
				counter.Update();
			}
			return counter.NextId;
        }
		else if (counterKey == "scheduleId") {
            var counter = ScheduleIdCounter.Query().FirstOrDefault();
			if (counter == null) {
				counter = new ScheduleIdCounter { NextId = 1 };
				counter.Insert();
			} else {
				counter.NextId++;
				counter.Update();
			}
			return counter.NextId;
        }
		else if (counterKey == "employeeId") {
            var counter = EmployeeIdCounter.Query().FirstOrDefault();
			if (counter == null) {
				counter = new EmployeeIdCounter { NextId = 1 };
				counter.Insert();
			} else {
				counter.NextId++;
				counter.Update();
			}
			return counter.NextId;
        }
		else if (counterKey == "jobId") {
           var counter = JobIdCounter.Query().FirstOrDefault();
			if (counter == null) {
				counter = new JobIdCounter { NextId = 1 };
				counter.Insert();
			} else {
				counter.NextId++;
				counter.Update();
			}
			return counter.JobId;
        }
		else if (counterKey == "ticketId") {
           var counter = TicketIdCounter.Query().FirstOrDefault();
			if (counter == null) {
				counter = new TicketIdCounter { NextId = 1 };
				counter.Insert();
			} else {
				counter.NextId++;
				counter.Update();
			}
			return counter.NextId;
        }
		else if (counterKey == "saleId") {

				counter = new SaleIdCounter { NextId = 1 };
				counter.Insert();
			} else {
				counter.NextId++;

           var counter = LogIdCounter.Query().FirstOrDefault();

			return counter.NextId;
        } else {
            return 0;
        }

C#
Important Notes on Table Definitions:

Identity: The UserProfile table uses Identity as its primary key. This is required for SpacetimeDB's authentication system. You will not use a numeric UserId as the primary key for UserProfile.

LegacyUserId: The UserProfile table includes a LegacyUserId field. This will store the original long UserId from your SQL Server database. This is crucial for maintaining compatibility with your existing API and client applications during the migration. It has the [Column(ColumnAttrs.Unique)] attribute to enforce uniqueness.

Auto-Incrementing IDs: For other tables (like Bus, Route, Ticket), we use uint as the primary key type. SpacetimeDB does not have built-in auto-incrementing IDs. We use the atomic counter pattern (separate tables like BusIdCounter) and the GetNextId helper function to generate unique IDs.

No Foreign Key Constraints: SpacetimeDB doesn't enforce foreign keys. You'll need to validate relationships within your reducer logic (I'll show this in the reducer examples).

Data Types: I've used appropriate SpacetimeDB data types. Note the use of ulong for timestamps (milliseconds since the Unix epoch). decimal is not supported; use double for currency.

Arrays: SpacetimeDB does support arrays of primitive types. I've used string[] in RouteSchedule for RouteStops, DaysOfWeek, etc. This is a good fit for your data.

Denormalization: I've included an example of denormalization (BusModel in Route). This can improve query performance by avoiding the need to query multiple tables. You can add other denormalized fields as needed.

Required Attribute: I've removed most of the explicit [Required] attributes that you had on the SQL models. In SpacetimeDB, fields within structs are implicitly required unless you make them nullable (e.g., string?, ulong?). SpacetimeDB does not allow null values in non-primary key fields unless they are explicitly nullable. Only add ? if a field can truly be missing.

No Navigation Properties: SpacetimeDB doesn't use navigation properties like EF Core. Relationships are managed through explicit foreign key fields (like DriverId, BusId in the Route table) and queries.

Step 3: Implement Reducers (C#)

Reducers are the only way to modify data in SpacetimeDB. They are C# functions that run on the server. This ensures data consistency and atomicity. All reducers should be inside your Module class.

I'll provide complete, ready-to-use reducer examples for the most critical operations. I'll include:

Input Validation: Checking for nulls, empty strings, valid ranges, etc.

Relationship Enforcement: Checking that related records exist (e.g., checking if a RouteId is valid before creating a Ticket).

Authorization: Basic authorization checks (e.g., checking if the caller has the "admin" role). You'll need to adapt this to your specific permission system.

Error Handling: Throwing SpacetimeDBException for errors.

Atomic Counter Usage: Using the GetNextId function for auto-incrementing IDs.

Timestamp Handling: Using ctx.Time.ToUnixTimeMilliseconds() for timestamps.

Transactionality - because reducers are transactions and are atomic

Here's a substantial set of reducers to get you started, covering user management, roles, permissions, and some basic fleet and ticket operations. This is not exhaustive, but it shows the patterns you'll use for all your other reducers.

Currently, SpacetimeDB has limited built-in permission support 1:

Tables can be marked as private or public using:
csharp
[SpacetimeDB.Table(Public = true)]
Private tables (default) can only be accessed by the module owner
Public tables are readable by all users but can only be modified through reducers
For implementing RBAC, you have two options:

Keep RBAC in your API layer:
Maintain existing ASP.NET Core authorization
Use SpacetimeDB just for data storage
API validates permissions before calling reducers
Implement RBAC in SpacetimeDB:
Create role/permission tables
Check permissions in reducers
More complex but gives you atomic operations
The SpacetimeDB team is actively working on row-level permissions 2, but it's not yet available.

In the client SDK, you must first subscribe to data before querying it 1:

csharp
// Subscribe to tables
SpacetimeDBClient.instance.Subscribe(new List<string> { "SELECT * FROM Role", "SELECT * FROM Permission" });
Then you can query using the generated methods :

csharp
// Find by ID
var role = Role.FindById(roleId);

// Filter by column
var permissions = Permission.FilterByName(permissionName); 
The code pattern you showed:

csharp
var bus = SpacetimeDB.Query<Bus>()
    .Where(b => b.busId == busId)
    .FirstOrDefault();
Is not valid according to the documentation. Instead, you should use the generated methods .

For implementing RBAC in SpacetimeDB, you would:

Define tables with proper attributes 2:
csharp
[SpacetimeDB.Table(Name = "role", Public = true)]
public partial struct Role {
    [SpacetimeDB.Column(ColumnAttrs.PrimaryKey)]
    public uint RoleId;
    public string Name;
}

[SpacetimeDB.Table(Name = "permission")] 
public partial struct Permission {
    [SpacetimeDB.Column(ColumnAttrs.PrimaryKey)]
    public uint PermissionId;
    public string Name;
}
Create reducers to check permissions 1:
csharp
[SpacetimeDB.Reducer] 
public static bool HasPermission(ReducerContext ctx, string permissionName)
{
    var userRoles = UserRole.FilterByUserId(ctx.CallerIdentity);
    foreach(var userRole in userRoles) {
        var rolePermissions = RolePermission.FilterByRoleId(userRole.RoleId);
        foreach(var rp in rolePermissions) {
            var permission = Permission.FindById(rp.PermissionId);
            if(permission.Name == permissionName) {
                return true;
            }
        }
    }
    return false;
}
Use permission checks in other reducers :
csharp
[SpacetimeDB.Reducer]
public static void CreateBus(ReducerContext ctx, string model)
{
    if (!HasPermission(ctx, "CREATE_BUS")) {
        throw new Exception("Unauthorized");
    }
    
    // Create bus logic here
}
The key differences from SQL-based RBAC:

All permission checks happen in reducers
No JOIN operations - must query tables separately
Must subscribe to relevant tables in client
All operations are atomic within reducers

## 3. Functional Specifications

### 3.1. Authorization System

#### Enhanced Role-Based Access Control
- **Granular Permission System**
  - Role hierarchy with inheritance support
  - Custom claims for feature-specific permissions
  - Dynamic permission management
  - Role-based menu visibility

- **Permission Categories**
  - System Administration
  - User Management
  - Transport Management
  - Ticket Operations
  - Report Generation
  - Configuration Management

#### Authentication Flow
1. **Initial Authentication**
   - User provides credentials
   - System validates against stored hashed passwords
   - JWT token issued with role claims
   - Refresh token generated and stored

2. **Token Management**
   - Access token validation on each request
   - Automatic refresh token rotation
   - Token revocation on logout
   - Session management

3. **Security Features**
   - Brute force protection
   - IP-based rate limiting
   - Device fingerprinting
   - Audit logging

### 3.2. Administrator Module

#### User Management
- **Account Operations**
  - CRUD operations for user accounts
  - Bulk user import/export
  - Password reset workflow
  - Account lockout management

- **Role Management**
  - Role creation and assignment
  - Permission template management
  - Role hierarchy configuration
  - Custom claim management

- **Audit System**
  - Detailed action logging
  - Change tracking
  - Session monitoring

Core Authorization Reducers:
csharp
public static class AuthReducers
{
    [SpacetimeDB.Reducer]
    public static void RegisterUser(ReducerContext ctx, string login, string passwordHash, string email)
    {
        // Check if user exists
        var existingUser = User.LoginIndex.Filter(login).FirstOrDefault();
        if (existingUser != null)
        {
            throw new Exception("User already exists");
        }

        var user = new User
        {
            identity = ctx.Sender,
            login = login,
            passwordHash = passwordHash,
            email = email,
            isActive = true,
            createdAt = ctx.Time,
            lastLoginAt = 0
        };
        user.Insert();

        // Assign default role
        var defaultRole = Role.NameIndex.Filter("User").FirstOrDefault();
        if (defaultRole != null)
        {
            var userRole = new UserRole
            {
                userIdentity = ctx.Sender,
                roleId = defaultRole.roleId
            };
            userRole.Insert();
        }
    }

    [SpacetimeDB.Reducer]
    public static bool HasPermission(ReducerContext ctx, string permissionName)
    {
        var userRoles = UserRole.UserIdentityIndex.Filter(ctx.Sender);
        
        foreach (var userRole in userRoles)
        {
            var rolePermissions = RolePermission.RoleIdIndex.Filter(userRole.roleId);
            foreach (var rolePermission in rolePermissions)
            {
                var permission = Permission.FindById(rolePermission.permissionId);
                if (permission.name == permissionName && permission.isActive)
                {
                    return true;
                }
            }
        }
        return false;
    }
}
Ticket Management Reducers:
csharp
public static class TicketReducers
{
    [SpacetimeDB.Reducer]
    public static void PurchaseTicket(ReducerContext ctx, uint routeId, string seatNumber)
    {
        // Check permissions
        if (!AuthReducers.HasPermission(ctx, "PURCHASE_TICKET"))
        {
            throw new Exception("Unauthorized: Missing PURCHASE_TICKET permission");
        }

        // Validate route
        var route = Route.FindById(routeId);
        if (route == null)
        {
            throw new Exception("Route not found");
        }

        // Check seat availability
        var existingTicket = Ticket.SeatIndex.Filter((routeId, seatNumber)).FirstOrDefault();
        if (existingTicket != null)
        {
            throw new Exception("Seat already taken");
        }

        // Create ticket
        var ticket = new Ticket
        {
            routeId = routeId,
            seatNumber = seatNumber,
            status = 1, // Active
            purchasedBy = ctx.Sender,
            departureTime = ctx.Time + 3600, // Example: departure in 1 hour
            price = CalculateTicketPrice(route)
        };
        ticket.Insert();
    }

    [SpacetimeDB.Reducer]
    public static void CancelTicket(ReducerContext ctx, uint ticketId)
    {
        var ticket = Ticket.FindById(ticketId);
        if (ticket == null)
        {
            throw new Exception("Ticket not found");
        }

        // Only ticket owner or admin can cancel
        if (ticket.purchasedBy != ctx.Sender && !AuthReducers.HasPermission(ctx, "ADMIN_CANCEL_TICKET"))
        {
            throw new Exception("Unauthorized: Cannot cancel other user's ticket");
        }

        ticket.status = 2; // Cancelled
        Ticket.UpdateById(ticketId, ticket);
    }
}
Fleet Management Reducers:
csharp
public static class FleetReducers
{
    [SpacetimeDB.Reducer]
    public static void AddBus(ReducerContext ctx, string model, uint seats, string regNumber)
    {
        if (!AuthReducers.HasPermission(ctx, "MANAGE_FLEET"))
        {
            throw new Exception("Unauthorized: Missing MANAGE_FLEET permission");
        }

        var bus = new Bus
        {
            model = model,
            seats = seats,
            registrationNumber = regNumber,
            status = 1, // Active
            manufactureYear = 2024,
            lastMaintenanceDate = ctx.Time,
            nextMaintenanceDate = ctx.Time + (90 * 24 * 3600) // 90 days
        };
        bus.Insert();
    }

    [SpacetimeDB.Reducer]
    public static void ScheduleMaintenance(ReducerContext ctx, uint busId, ulong maintenanceDate)
    {
        if (!AuthReducers.HasPermission(ctx, "SCHEDULE_MAINTENANCE"))
        {
            throw new Exception("Unauthorized: Missing SCHEDULE_MAINTENANCE permission");
        }

        var bus = Bus.FindById(busId);
        if (bus == null)
        {
            throw new Exception("Bus not found");
        }

        bus.nextMaintenanceDate = maintenanceDate;
        Bus.UpdateById(busId, bus);
    }
}

ulong for timestamps

Table.Insert()
Table.FindById()

Index.Filter()

Permission checking in each reducer
Role-based access control through table relationships

No direct SQL queries:
Using table-generated methods
Using indexes for efficient queries
Relationships managed in code

uhh how do SpacetimeDB's generated methods even function \
From the documentation, SpacetimeDB generates methods for tables in C# like this:

csharp
[SpacetimeDB.Table]
public partial struct Person
{
    [SpacetimeDB.Column(ColumnAttrs.PrimaryKey)]
    public int Id;
    public string Name;
    public int Age;
}
This generates the following methods 1:

csharp
public partial struct Person
{
    // Insert current instance into table
    public void Insert();

    // Iterate all rows
    public static IEnumerable<Person> Iter();

    // Query with filter expression
    public static IEnumerable<Person> Query(Expression<Func<Person, bool>> filter);

    // Generated for each column:
    public static IEnumerable<Person> FilterByName(string name);
    public static IEnumerable<Person> FilterByAge(int age);

    // For unique/primary key columns:
    public static Person? FindById(int id);
    public static bool DeleteById(int id);
    public static bool UpdateById(int oldId, Person newValue);
}
So when you define a table, SpacetimeDB automatically generates these methods for querying and modifying the data .

For example, to find a user by ID you would do:

csharp
var user = User.FindById(userId);
Rather than writing SQL queries or using Entity Framework .

The key points about these generated methods:

They are created at compile time
They provide type-safe access to the data
They handle all the database operations internally
They use SpacetimeDB's indexing system for performance
Would you like me to explain any specific generated method in more detail?

Ah, you're right! We can create a hybrid approach where we keep the ASP.NET API server as a facade while using SpacetimeDB as the backend. Here's how:

First, define the SpacetimeDB tables and reducers:
csharp
[SpacetimeDB.Table]
public partial struct User 
{
    [PrimaryKey]
    public Identity identity;
    public string login;
    public string passwordHash;
    public string email;
    public bool isActive;
    public ulong createdAt;
}

[SpacetimeDB.Table]
public partial struct AuthToken 
{
    [PrimaryKey]
    public string token;
    public Identity userIdentity;
    public ulong expiresAt;
}
Create authentication reducers:
csharp
public static class AuthReducers 
{
    [SpacetimeDB.Reducer]
    public static void CreateAuthToken(ReducerContext ctx, string token, ulong expiresAt)
    {
        var authToken = new AuthToken {
            token = token,
            userIdentity = ctx.Sender,
            expiresAt = expiresAt
        };
        authToken.Insert();
    }

    [SpacetimeDB.Reducer]
    public static void ValidateCredentials(ReducerContext ctx, string login, string passwordHash)
    {
        var user = User.FilterByLogin(login).FirstOrDefault();
        if (user == null || user.passwordHash != passwordHash)
        {
            throw new Exception("Invalid credentials");
        }
    }
}
Modify the existing AuthController to work with SpacetimeDB:
csharp
[ApiController]
[Route("api/[controller]")]
public class AuthController : ControllerBase
{
    private readonly ISpacetimeDBClient _spacetimeDB;
    private readonly IConfiguration _configuration;

    public AuthController(ISpacetimeDBClient spacetimeDB, IConfiguration configuration)
    {
        _spacetimeDB = spacetimeDB;
        _configuration = configuration;
    }

    [Route("login")]
    [HttpPost]
    [AllowAnonymous]
    public async Task<ActionResult<string>> Login([FromBody] LoginModel model)
    {
        try 
        {
            // First validate credentials in SpacetimeDB
            await _spacetimeDB.CallReducer("ValidateCredentials", model.Login, HashPassword(model.Password));

            // If validation succeeds, generate JWT token
            var token = GenerateJwtToken(model.Login);

            // Store token in SpacetimeDB
            var expiresAt = DateTimeOffset.UtcNow.AddHours(1).ToUnixTimeMilliseconds();
            await _spacetimeDB.CallReducer("CreateAuthToken", token, expiresAt);

            return Ok(new { token });
        }
        catch (Exception ex)
        {
            return Unauthorized(new { message = "Invalid username or password" });
        }
    }

    private string GenerateJwtToken(string login)
    {
        // Keep your existing JWT generation logic
        var tokenHandler = new JwtSecurityTokenHandler();
        var key = Encoding.ASCII.GetBytes(_configuration["JwtSettings:Secret"]);
        var tokenDescriptor = new SecurityTokenDescriptor
        {
            Subject = new ClaimsIdentity(new[]
            {
                new Claim(ClaimTypes.Name, login)
            }),
            Expires = DateTime.UtcNow.AddHours(1),
            SigningCredentials = new SigningCredentials(
                new SymmetricSecurityKey(key), 
                SecurityAlgorithms.HmacSha256Signature)
        };

        var token = tokenHandler.CreateToken(tokenDescriptor);
        return tokenHandler.WriteToken(token);
    }
}
Add SpacetimeDB client configuration in Startup.cs:
csharp
public void ConfigureServices(IServiceCollection services)
{
    // Existing configurations
    services.AddControllers();
    services.AddAuthentication(JwtBearerDefaults.AuthenticationScheme)
        .AddJwtBearer(/* your existing JWT config */);

    // Add SpacetimeDB client
    services.AddSingleton<ISpacetimeDBClient>(sp =>
    {
        var config = sp.GetRequiredService<IConfiguration>();
        return new SpacetimeDBClient(config["SpacetimeDB:Address"]);
    });
}
Create a middleware to validate tokens against SpacetimeDB:
csharp
public class SpacetimeDBAuthMiddleware
{
    private readonly RequestDelegate _next;
    private readonly ISpacetimeDBClient _spacetimeDB;

    public SpacetimeDBAuthMiddleware(RequestDelegate next, ISpacetimeDBClient spacetimeDB)
    {
        _next = next;
        _spacetimeDB = spacetimeDB;
    }

    public async Task InvokeAsync(HttpContext context)
    {
        var token = context.Request.Headers["Authorization"]
            .FirstOrDefault()?.Split(" ").Last();

        if (token != null)
        {
            // Query SpacetimeDB for token validity
            var authToken = await _spacetimeDB.Query<AuthToken>()
                .Where(t => t.token == token && t.expiresAt > DateTimeOffset.UtcNow.ToUnixTimeMilliseconds())
                .FirstOrDefaultAsync();

            if (authToken != null)
            {
                // Token is valid in SpacetimeDB
                context.Items["UserIdentity"] = authToken.userIdentity;
            }
        }

        await _next(context);
    }
}
This hybrid approach:

Keeps your existing API endpoints and JWT authentication
Uses SpacetimeDB for data storage and validation
Maintains compatibility with your existing client
Allows gradual migration to SpacetimeDB
You can gradually move more functionality to SpacetimeDB reducers while keeping the API facade for client compatibility.

how does SpacetimeDB.Query in client sdk code work
For the C# client SDK, querying works through generated methods for each table. Here's how:

First you need to subscribe to the table data you want to query:
csharp
SpacetimeDBClient.instance.Subscribe(new List<string> { "SELECT * FROM User" });
1

Once subscribed, you can query the table using generated methods:
csharp
// Iterate all rows
foreach (var user in User.Iter()) {
    Console.WriteLine($"User: {user.Name}");
}
For filtering by specific columns, the SDK generates methods like:
csharp
// Filter by column value
public static IEnumerable<TABLE> FilterBySender(COLUMNTYPE value);
For unique/primary key columns, you get find methods:
csharp
// Find by unique column
public static TABLE? FindBySender(COLUMNTYPE value);
The key points about querying in SpacetimeDB:

You must first subscribe to the data you want to query
The SDK maintains a local client cache of subscribed data
All operations work only on the subscribed data in the cache
SpacetimeDB does not support foreign key constraints, so you need to manually subscribe to all related tables
The documentation recommends optimizing network performance by selecting as few rows as possible in your Subscribe query. Operations that need the entire database state are better run inside modules .

Would you like me to explain any specific aspect of querying in more detail?

The SpacetimeDB C# client SDK

so check and analyze this whole text Okay, I've reviewed the messagespacetime.txt file, SpacetimeDB documentation, and our prior discussion. I'll create a comprehensive, step-by-step guide for migrating your SQL Server-based API server to SpacetimeDB, keeping your existing authentication/authorization system intact (for now), and minimizing disruption to your client applications. This will be a hybrid approach, focusing on a gradual, iterative transition.

CRITICAL UNDERSTANDINGS (REITERATED):

SpacetimeDB is NOT a drop-in replacement for SQL Server. It's a fundamentally different architecture. This means no ORM (EF Core), no foreign keys, no joins, and all data modifications happen through reducers.

Reducers are EVERYTHING. All inserts, updates, and deletes must go through reducers. Reducers are C# functions that run inside the SpacetimeDB server, ensuring data consistency and atomicity.

Identity is for USERS. The built-in Identity type is specifically for user authentication and session management within SpacetimeDB. Do not use it for things like BusId, RouteId, TicketId, etc. Use uint for those.

No automatic RBAC. SpacetimeDB does not have a built-in role-based access control system (yet). You'll implement your own using tables (like Role, Permission, UserRole, RolePermission) and enforce authorization checks within your reducers.

No Joins: Because SpacetimeDB uses structs and the documentation never mentions Join operations, we cannot use Joins in spacetimedb

Hybrid Approach is ESSENTIAL. We will initially dual-write to both SQL Server (using your existing EF Core code) and SpacetimeDB (using reducers). This allows for:

Validation: You can compare the data in both databases to ensure consistency.

Rollback: If something goes wrong with SpacetimeDB, you can easily fall back to SQL Server.

Gradual Migration: You can migrate controllers and client application functionality one piece at a time.

Legacy ID Preservation: We'll add Legacy{Entity}Id fields (e.g., LegacyUserId, LegacyRoleId) to your SpacetimeDB tables to store your original SQL Server primary keys. This allows your existing client code (which might use these numeric IDs) to continue working during the migration.

API Facade: Your ASP.NET Core API will initially act as a facade over SpacetimeDB. Clients will continue to use the same API endpoints and JWT authentication. The API server will translate these requests into SpacetimeDB reducer calls and queries.

Migration Steps:

Step 1: Project Setup and SpacetimeDB Installation
